agreement: General direct compressed-code to native-MMA format and RoPE-aware codebooks have strong prior work.
Large-query native-MMA support missing in a public implementation alone is insufficient novelty or utility evidence.
Prepared caching is a strong simple baseline with explicitly higher resident-byte cost.
No new method or GPU experiment adopted in this scope.
corrections_preserved: Observed Sage1 used FP16 V, not unmeasured FP8 V.
Payload smaller than GPU capacity does not prove whole-model fit.
Equal bytes or explicit memory-time-quality cost points matter even without a binding memory cap.
L2-normalization commuting with RoPE does not imply quantization commutes.
CommVQ examined public kernel is single-query BF16/1-bit-V, not proof the large-query INT8/FP8 boundary is fully solved.
